definitions.explanation: The quality of being good; the good points or appeal of something. The noun form of the adjective {良|よ}い.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}の{良|よ}さを{伝|つた}えたい。
examples.english: I want to convey the appeal of this town.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}ってみて、はじめてこの{道具|どうぐ}の{良|よ}さがわかった。
examples.english: Only after trying it did I understand how good this tool is.

examples.japanese: {木|き}でできた{家具|かぐ}の{良|よ}さは、{時間|じかん}が{経|た}つほど{味|あじ}わいが{増|ま}すところにある。
examples.english: The appeal of wooden furniture lies in how its character deepens as time passes.

notes:
The noun form of the adjective {良|よ}い / いい (good), formed by replacing the final い with さ. Expresses the degree or quality of goodness, or the merits of something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {良|よ}さを{伝|つた}える: to convey the appeal (of something)
- {良|よ}さが{分|わ}かる: to appreciate the good points
- {良|よ}さを{生|い}かす: to make the most of a strength

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {長所|ちょうしょ}: strong point; merit — a specific good feature, more concrete
- {魅力|みりょく}: charm; appeal — emphasizes attractiveness rather than plain quality
